text:
{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system treats past interactions as broad interest in related products or media, with insufficient distinction between general affinity and a current reason to choose.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations align when they continue a specific artist, listening theme, or recognizable subject supported by history.",
    "Practical recommendations align when they complement existing equipment or extend a demonstrated repair, storage, or connectivity need."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broadly related items compete with stronger matches despite requiring an unexpressed project, different listening mood, or unconfirmed equipment.",
    "Repeated capabilities, familiar titles, and multiple similar alternatives are treated as further opportunities without enough evidence of replacement need or additional value.",
    "Sparse or unidentified histories appear to support broader preference assumptions than the available evidence warrants."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Shared product category, brand ecosystem, genre, or compilation wording substitutes for a specific functional or musical connection.",
    "Similarity to previous purchases is treated as sufficient evidence of next-item relevance, including redundant or overly specialized products."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Recent activity and repeated coherent interests provide stronger clues to current purpose, mood, and preferred artists than isolated interactions.",
    "Ownership, compatibility, dimensions, and manageable quantities determine whether a related product is actually useful.",
    "Users choose selectively among plausible matches, favoring a clear immediate benefit or recognizable content connection."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "Broad affinity places plausible but weakly motivated items near the top, leaving too few recommendations with a specific, timely reason to choose.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The share of top-ranked recommendations users would choose now, distinguished from items they merely consider related or appealing.",
    "The frequency of top-ranked rejections attributed to redundancy, incompatible equipment, excessive quantity, or an unexpressed task or mood.",
    "The frequency with which users prefer a lower-ranked item because it better matches recent activity or a specific recurring interest.",
    "The frequency of indeterminate relevance judgments when available history or item information cannot establish a personal connection."
  ]
}
